MedSynapse Interactive Content Assistant

Setup and user guide for medical writers

Version 1.2 · October 2026 · Maintained by Kaushik Desai

1. What this is, and how long setup takes

The MedSynapse Interactive Content Assistant is a tool that works inside Claude. You give it your article (a Word file or a PDF), answer a few questions, and it turns the article into short, visual, clickable content that you paste into TinyMCE on MedSynapse. It follows our component library and uses only the text in your source.

Setup takes about 15 to 20 minutes, once. After that, each article takes a few minutes of your time.

Part

What you do

A

Create a free GitHub account (skip if you already have one).

B

Send your GitHub username to the admin and accept the invitation.

C

Connect the assistant to Claude.

D

Make your first interactive content.

E

Revise, check and paste into TinyMCE.

Why GitHub? The assistant and its component library are stored in a private GitHub repository (an online project folder). Being invited to it gives you the latest version automatically.

How the pieces connect: admin, GitHub, Claude, TinyMCE and the public assets repository.

2. Before you start

Have these ready:

  • A Claude account (claude.ai) that you can sign in to. Free, Pro, Max and Team plans all work.
  • A work or personal email address you can open during setup.
  • Your source article as a Word or PDF file.
  • Only if you want images: the AWS link for each image. Without links, the assistant puts the information from images into components instead.

3. Part A: Create a GitHub account

Already have a GitHub account? Skip to Part B and use that account's username.

1
Open github.com in your browser and click Sign up.
2
Enter your email address and click Continue. Use an address you check regularly: the invitation will arrive there.
3
Create a password. Use a long one that you do not use anywhere else.
4
Choose a username. Short and professional is best. Write it down: you will send it to the admin.
5
Complete the small verification puzzle, then click Create account.
6
GitHub emails you a launch code. Open the email, copy the code and paste it into the page.

GitHub changes its screens now and then, so wording may differ slightly. The path is always the same: sign up, verify your email, pick the free plan.

4. Part B: Get access to the repository

4.1 Send your username to the admin

1
Send your GitHub username and the email address you used to Kaushik Desai (admin), by email or chat.
2
Say which Claude plan you are on, if you know it (Free, Pro, Max or Team).
3
The admin adds you as a collaborator. This takes a minute. The admin will tell you when it is done.

4.2 Accept the invitation

1
Check your email. You will receive a message from GitHub: invited you to collaborate on desaikaushik1997/medsyn-interactive.
2
Click View invitation, sign in to GitHub if asked, then click Accept invitation.
3
Check it worked: open https://github.com/desaikaushik1997/medsyn-interactive while signed in. You should see the project files. If you see "404" or "Page not found", the invitation has not been accepted yet, or you are signed in with a different account.

No email? Look in your spam folder. Or, while signed in to GitHub, open https://github.com/desaikaushik1997/medsyn-interactive/invitations. You can also click the bell icon at the top right of GitHub. Invitations expire after seven days, so ask the admin to resend if needed.

5. Part C: Connect the assistant to Claude

Your plan

Route

Updates

Free, Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise

Plugin (recommended)

You get updates from the repository

5.1 Add the plugin

1
Sign in at claude.ai (or open the Claude desktop app).
2
In the left sidebar click Customize, then open the Plugins tab.
3
Click Add, then choose Add marketplace.
4
Choose Add from a repository.
5
Type desaikaushik1997/medsyn-interactive and continue.
6
If Claude asks you to connect your GitHub account, agree and sign in with the same GitHub account that accepted the invitation. This lets Claude read the private repository.
7
If you see a sync option for this repository, switch it on: it keeps your copy up to date.
8
Click Done. Then find medsyn-interactive in the list and make sure it is turned on or you might have to click Add in front of that plugin.
9
Check it: open a new chat, type / or click the + button, and look for medsyn-interactive. You should see its actions (convert, edit, revise, finalize).

6. Part D: Make your first interactive content

The writer's steps, from attaching the article to pasting into TinyMCE, and the three ways to change it afterwards.

6.1 Start a chat

1
Open a new chat for each article. (Do not reuse a chat from another article.)
2
Attach your Word or PDF file with the paperclip or the + button.
3
Type: Use the medsyn-interactive skill to turn this article into interactive content.

Naming the skill in your first message makes Claude pick it every time. You can also type / and choose the convert action if you are on the plugin route.

6.2 Claude reads your article, then shows a "look picker"

Claude reads the whole article once. Then it creates a small page called palette-preview.html and asks you to open it. It shows 24 numbered colour palettes, seven layouts (A to G) and seven tap styles (0 to 6). Use the three buttons at the top (Palette, Layout, Tap cue) to jump between the parts. Open the file in your browser (click it in the chat), decide, and come back to the chat. You can also look at the same pages beforehand online: see Part G.

The look picker (palette-preview.html). Use the buttons at the top to jump to Palette, Layout or Tap cue.

Layouts A to G. Pick one letter.

Tap cues 0 to 6. The demos are live: click them to see how they behave.

6.3 Claude asks a few questions, all in one message

Answer all of them in one reply. Skip any you do not care about: Claude uses the default shown in brackets.

Question

What it means

Example answer

1. Format

The type of content. Today: Interactive article.

Interactive article

2. Audience

Who reads it. Changes the tone of components.

HCP

3. Look: palette

A number from the picker, or your own colours (a Coolors link or hex codes), or client brand colours. Default: library blue and pink.

Palette 4

3. Look: layout

A Classic (white cards), B Tinted (coloured sections), C Banded (colour header bars), D Clean (thin accent edge), E Top rule (heavy coloured top edge), F Editorial (big numbers, open look), G Stepper (numbered rail, good for processes). Default A.

Layout C

3. Look: tap cue

How readers know a card opens. 0 plain arrow, 1 subtle row, 2 pulse chevron (soft pulse on the first card only, recommended), 3 TAP chips (only if the client asks), 4 ripple row, 5 solid rows with a white ripple, 6 arrow trail. Levels 2, 4, 5 and 6 animate only the first card of a group.

Tap cue 2

4. Introduction

Include your intro? Which intro style? References and abbreviations? Default: leave the intro out.

Leave the intro out. Include references and abbreviations.

5. Density

Concise (short) or fuller.

Concise

6. Images

Only if you give AWS links will images be used. Otherwise data inside images becomes components.

No images

A complete reply could look like this:

Format: interactive article. Audience: HCP. Palette 4, layout C, tap cue 2. Leave the intro out; include references and abbreviations. Concise. No images.

Client brand colours? Say so here: "Use the client's brand colours: #003B71 and #E4002B" or attach the brand guideline page. Claude checks that the text stays readable on those colours.

6.4 Review the plan, then approve

Before building anything, Claude shows a plan table: for each section of your article, which component it will use, what it keeps, what it leaves out, and how citations are handled. Check it:

  • Does each section use a sensible component?
  • Is anything important left out?
  • Are the numbers and citations assigned to the right sections?

To approve, reply Looks good, go ahead. To change something, say what, for example: For section 3 use a timeline instead of cards, and keep the bar chart for section 5. Claude updates the plan and asks again.

6.5 The result and the hand-off report

Claude builds the content, checks it automatically against our TinyMCE rules, fixes problems itself, and saves a file named like your-article-interactive.html. Then it gives a short hand-off report. Read it:

Report item

What to do

Components used

Check the structure matches what you expected.

What was left out, and why

Make sure nothing essential was dropped.

Citations

It says "unchanged" or shows an old to new number table. If numbers changed, check your reference list.

Data taken from images

Check each figure against the original.

Needs your input

Things Claude will not invent: the introduction, references, missing citations, image links. Provide them or add them in TinyMCE.

Needs human review

Anything the checker could not safely fix. Pass it to the admin if you are unsure.

6.6 What the assistant will never do

  • It will not invent facts, numbers, quiz questions, myths, patient statements, references or links. Everything comes from your source, because content goes to MLR.
  • It will not add images unless you give a link.
  • It will not rewrite your wording beyond shortening it. If you want wording changed, say so.

You are still the author. Always compare the output with your source before it goes to MLR. The assistant is a fast first draft with built-in checks, not a replacement for review.

7. Part E: Revise, check and publish

7.1 Paste into TinyMCE

1
Open your .html file in Notepad (Windows) or TextEdit (Mac), or with the file preview in Claude. You will see lines that start COPY FROM HERE and COPY TO HERE.
2
Select everything between those two comment lines (include them or not) and copy it.
3
In TinyMCE, click the source code button, which looks like </> (an angle-bracket and slash symbol). Do not paste into the normal visual view.
4
Paste once, as one block. Do not add blank lines. Click Save in the source code window.
5
Check the result on a desktop and on a phone-size window before publishing.

Never add blank lines between pasted pieces, and never paste the content twice. TinyMCE turns blank lines into empty paragraphs that add unwanted space.

7.2 Change one thing: Edit

In the same chat, attach the file if needed and write exactly what to change. Claude changes only that and nothing else.

You say

What happens

Edit: change the heading of section 2 to "Fluid management"

One heading changes.

Edit: in the results rows, change 26.8% to 27.1%

One number changes (and the bar if needed).

(screenshot with a circle) Edit: change this sentence to "..."

Claude says what it found, then changes it.

If your instruction could match several places, Claude asks which one. Answer briefly: The second one.

7.3 Apply a list of reviewer comments: Revise

1
Attach the current .html file and the comments (paste them, or attach the Word or PDF with the comments).
2
Type: Use the medsyn-interactive skill in revise mode. Apply these MLR comments.
3
Claude makes a numbered change list, one row per comment, and asks only about comments that are unclear, contradict each other, or need content that is not in your source.
4
It applies the clear ones and saves a new version (your old file is kept).
5
It reports each comment as done or not done, with the exact before and after. Comments that ask for content outside your source are listed as not applied: send Claude the source text or reference and ask again.

7.4 Final check before publishing: Finalize

When everything is approved, type: Finalize this for TinyMCE. Claude removes anything TinyMCE would break without touching your wording or design, and reports PASS. Paste that final file.

Use component 52 (forest plot) for the hazard ratios in section 4.

Add an animated element

Add one animated element, for example a heartbeat divider before section 3.

Change one thing

Edit: [exactly what to change and where]

Apply reviewer comments

Use revise mode. Apply these MLR comments: [paste or attach]

Last check before publishing

Finalize this for TinyMCE.

See what is available

Which components can you use for trial results data?

Fix a wrong colour

Edit: use #003B71 instead of the blue everywhere.

Choose the look straight away

Palette 20, layout E, tap cue 4.

9. Part F: Keeping up to date

How an update goes from the admin to the writers.

  • Plugin: when the admin announces an update, click Customize -> Plugins -> Yours -> click the dropdown besides Add

    Then click Manage marketplace
  • Click the 3 dots and then click Check for updates
  • Then click Done

After an update, start a new chat: chats that were already open keep using the old version. To check which library version you have, ask: Run the catalogue and tell me the library version.

10. Part G: The component gallery

The gallery is a web page that shows every component as a live preview, with a short "use when" note. Use it to decide which components suit your article before you start, and to find component numbers.

1
Open the MedSynapse library page: https://desaikaushik1997.github.io/medsyn-assets/ (save it as a bookmark). It always shows the latest published version; the version number is at the bottom-right of the page.

The library page. Open Component gallery or Palettes, layouts and tap cues.

2
Open Component gallery to see every component and animation as a live preview, and Palettes, layouts and tap cues to see all 24 palettes, layouts A to G and tap cues 0 to 6. Take a look and understand which interactive elements you can use before you write to Claude.

The component gallery: search box, category buttons and the Phone / Desktop switch.

The Animation library tab shows every animation and which components use it.

3
Use the search box, the category buttons (for example Data views, Clinical, Animated) and the Phone / Desktop switch.
4
Look for the labels on each card: Animated, Tap to open, and Needs figures from the source (the component only works if your article contains the numbers).
5
Note the number of components you like and tell Claude: Use components 52 and 59 where they fit.

11. Tips for the free plan and for saving usage

  • One article per chat. A long chat uses more of your allowance.
  • Answer all questions in one message instead of many short replies.
  • Do not ask Claude to paste the whole HTML into the chat. It saves the file for you.
  • Keep source files tidy: remove cover pages and long appendices you do not want converted.
  • If you hit a usage limit, wait for it to reset.

12. Troubleshooting

Problem

What to try

I see "404" on the repository page

Accept the invitation (Part B). Make sure you are signed in to the same GitHub account the admin invited.

I never got the invitation

Check spam, use the invitations link in Part B, or ask the admin to resend.

Claude refuses the repository when adding the plugin

Ask the admin or the organisation owner: plugin sources may be restricted, or your GitHub is not connected yet.

Claude does not seem to use the assistant

Name it in your message ("Use the medsyn-interactive skill..."). Check the plugin or skill toggle is on. Start a new chat.

Claude says it cannot run scripts or save files

Settings, Capabilities: turn on Code execution and file creation.

I cannot open palette-preview.html

Download the file and double-click it to open in your browser. Or ask Claude to list the options in text. You can also open the same page online (link in Part G).

TinyMCE changed how the content looks

Send the admin a screenshot and the TinyMCE source code.

Animations do not appear

They load from the internet. Check your connection. If the problem continues, tell the admin.

The content looks different on phone

That is expected for some layouts (cards stack). Check it on a phone-size window. Report real problems with a screenshot.

Something is wrong that I cannot fix

Send the admin: the chat link or a screenshot, the .html file, and what you expected.

Appendix A: Words used in this guide

Word

Meaning

GitHub

A website where our project files are stored and shared.

Repository

The online project folder on GitHub.

Collaborator

A person the admin has invited to the private repository.

Plugin

An add-on for Claude. Ours is the MedSynapse Interactive Content Assistant.

TinyMCE

The editor on MedSynapse where the content is pasted.

MLR

Medical, legal and regulatory review.

Source

Your original article. The assistant uses only text from it.
